target_customer: Homeowners seeking remodel and construction bids, and licensed contractors who pay for leads and tools
problem: Homeowners cannot easily judge contractor quality and price, and good contractors have little way to prove it.
business_model: Marketplace: contractors pay for leads and tools (the company later said you pay only when hired)
product_category: Contractor marketplace built on public license and permit data

founders.name: David Petersen
founders.background_notes: Santa Barbara Independent says he previously founded ImportGenius.

founders.name: Jiyan Wei
founders.background_notes: Described as a former product manager at Vocus who designed and built technology products.

competitors.name: Angie's List
competitors.what: Paid-membership reviews of local service providers

competitors.name: HomeAdvisor
competitors.what: Lead generation for home services that charged contractors for leads and referrals

technical_complexity.rationale: Harvesting, cleaning and matching about 125 million permits with license, bond and review records is real data engineering, though the marketplace on top is standard.

defensibility.rationale: The matched permit and license database plus marketplace history was slow to rebuild, but the underlying records are public and lead marketplaces are crowded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HomeAdvisor merged with Angie's List into ANGI Homeservices in 2017; BuildZoom survived independently and was sold to Block Renovation in November 2025.

market_need_then: Homeowners lacked data on contractors; Wei says he saw this after buying a home. Incumbents charged contractors for leads, and BuildZoom pitched free listings built on public records.

branding.domain_note: Operates at buildzoom.com; acquisition story not found.

rebrands.why: Press describes the acquired unit as BuildZoom Marketplace; no formal rebrand statement found.

branding.community_and_virality: No evidence of merch or community; coverage was startup and trade press.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive compound name that says what it does; no source shows brand-level pull beyond product coverage.

outcome_analysis: BuildZoom built a contractor marketplace on matched public permit and license data, raised about $14M across a 2013 seed, a 2014 extension and a 2015 Series A, and survived for twelve years against Angie's List and HomeAdvisor. It ended in a November 2025 sale of the marketplace to Block Renovation at an undisclosed price, so the outcome is a long-lived but modest exit with no stated valuation.
notes: buildzoom.com returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool. CB Insights totals $20.85M over 9 rounds, which is not itemized, so coverage is partial. One secondary source says Series A was $11M; the press release says $10.6M. Seed investors from search summary of TechCrunch coverage. Founder education not found. Block Renovation press coverage says the deal covered BuildZoom Marketplace; price undisclosed.
